headline: Chevron and Microsoft signed a 20-year deal in June for a Chevron gas power plant to supply a planned Microsoft data centre in West Texas.
score_reason: Pool score 7 lowered by 2: the deal dates from 22 Jun 2026 and EnergyNow re-dated it; the only newer fact is the 1 Oct Semafor report of a possible delay.
importance_line: It matters first to people around Pecos, where Microsoft says the campus would bring more than 6,000 construction jobs, then to Texas officials weighing data-centre permits, and to Chevron and Microsoft, but the project is not final until Chevron makes its investment decision, and a report says permit politics could delay that.
source: Data Center Knowledge, citing Chevron and Microsoft
summary: Data Center Knowledge reports, citing the companies, that on 22 Jun 2026 Chevron and Microsoft signed a 20-year agreement for a gas-fired power plant of about 2.67 gigawatts, built next to a planned Microsoft data centre near Pecos, Texas, with first power planned for 2028 and a final investment decision by Chevron still expected by the end of 2026. This is older news that EnergyNow re-published on 11 Oct 2026; the newest development is a Semafor report of 1 Oct, relayed by The Next Web, that state politics could push that decision into 2027 after Governor Greg Abbott's order pausing new environmental permits for data centres.
notes: Old news re-dated by EnergyNow (URL /2026/06/); hold back unless QA keeps it as a follow-up. Text read at Data Center Knowledge and The Next Web because the EnergyNow page returned 403. The Next Web discloses that its owner's marketplace lists Microsoft.
